text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Monetary Fund announced restoration and enhancement of Pakistan's suspended standby credit, increasing the total amount to be disbursed by an additional $231 million to $550 million until September next year.
- The provincial Sindh government withdrew charges against 40 activists of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
- A former deputy in the Punjab provincial assembly and his friend were shot dead by three unidentified men in Lahore.
- The adviser to the prime minister on finance and economic affairs Shahid Javed ials are worried about the long dry spell, which may adversely affect the wheat crop.

- The dollarisation of Pakistan's economy, measured by the ratio of resident foreign currency deposits against total domestic liquidity, rose steeply from 2.6 percent to about 14 percent in the first half of the 1990s.
- In an unprecedented move the World Bank has asked Pakistan for a third party inspectionow publication of names of people who have defaulted on loans or had them written off.
- The state-run Privatisation Commission will float its existing shares in the financial sector to introduce five million new investors to the stock market, its chairman Salman Shah said.
- The import trade price system has been restorre-shipment inspection.
